case_title: UGGARSAIN v. THE STATE OF HARYANA & ORS.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.304 Part-II, s.149; IPC s.148, s.323
aggravating_circumstances: Use of weapons, causing death, unlawful assembly
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment under s.302, one year rigorous imprisonment under s.148, and six months rigorous imprisonment under s.323
high_court_outcome: Partially allowed the appeal, converted conviction under s.302 to s.304 Part II, affirmed convictions under s.148 and s.323
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder (s.304 Part II) read with s.149
neutral_facts: The accused, eight individuals, were involved in a violent incident that resulted in the death of the victim. The incident occurred on the eve of Holika Dahan, where the accused, including Krishan and Brahmjit, attacked the victim and others with weapons. The victim sustained severe head injuries, leading to his death. The prosecution presented medical evidence, eyewitness accounts, and site plans to establish the incident. The trial court convicted all accused for causing death and injuries, sentencing them to life imprisonment and other terms. The High Court partially reduced the sentences for some accused, converting the conviction from murder to culpable homicide not amounting to murder, but maintaining convictions for other charges. The Supreme Court found the sentencing disparity inappropriate and modified the sentences for most accused, imposing a five-year term of rigorous imprisonment.
